0.value:
printable keeps only plain characters and drops everything else.

"Plain" here means the basic English keyboard set: the letters a to z and A to Z, the digits, ordinary punctuation, spaces, tabs and carriage returns. Everything outside that set is removed - other control characters and invisible formatting, but also every
accented letter, curly quotes, long dashes, symbols, emoji and every non-Latin script.

WHAT IT IS FOR:
Text that arrived from somewhere else - off a network, out of a file, from a speech service - and has things in it that are not really part of the text. Those are the strings that look correct and behave oddly: a comparison that fails, a width that is wrong, a word that will not match.

WHAT IT COSTS:
It does not translate anything, it deletes. "café" becomes "caf", a curly quoted word loses its quotes, and text in another language can vanish completely. Use it where plain English is what you expect; anywhere else it destroys the text.

A non-breaking space is removed too, not turned into a space, so the words on either side run together.

WHAT IT TAKES:
Anything; it is turned into a string first. A list of words is joined with spaces, a float is written with three decimals, and line breaks are removed. If nothing is left, nothing is sent.

SYNTAX:
printable

INPUTS:

characters in:
The text. Receiving it triggers the node.

OUTPUTS:

printable characters out:
What survives.

RELATED:
unescape_text turns HTML codes into characters - run it first, since printable would leave the codes behind as plain text.
string_replace to take out particular characters while keeping others.
